title: DPA - Output Provenance and User Consent Module (draft)
body:
Purpose and scope:
This module is intended as a negotiable attachment to Redwood Inference's standard Data Processing Agreement (DPA) for customers that require stronger contractual commitments around the provenance of model outputs and explicit handling of end-user consent signals. It is designed for regulated or high-sensitivity customers who need both (a) the ability to trace the lineage of a given inference result and (b) contractually-backed obligations about how end-user consent (where collected by the customer) affects processing, retention, and audit evidence.

Key principles (summary):
- Traceability: Redwood will maintain metadata sufficient to reconstruct the processing path for a discrete inference output for a limited retention period (see Retention below).
- Minimality: Provenance metadata will be scoped to what is necessary to reconstruct lineage (model id, model version, input hash, routing decision id, timestamp, and compliance flags) and not the full customer payload unless requested under audit.
- Consent-aware gating: If Customer provides Redwood with explicit end-user consent tokens or flags, Redwood will treat and surface those tokens for routing, retention, and audit according to the Customer's instructions and applicable law.
- Evidence and verification: Redwood will provide a defined audit package on request (see Audit & Evidence clause) to demonstrate handling consistent with contractual obligations.

Definitions (for this module):
- "Inference Output" means a model-generated response produced by the Service in response to a Customer request.
- "Provenance Metadata" means the non-content metadata recorded by Redwood that describes the processing path for an Inference Output, including model identifier and version, execution timestamp, routing decision identifier (e.g., fallback or variant used), quantization/precision profile, and a non-reversible hash of the input that preserves uniqueness without exposing raw input.
- "Consent Token" means an opaque value supplied by Customer that indicates that the underlying end-user has granted lawful basis for the specified processing, together with an optional scope payload (e.g., "analytics-only", "retain-temp", "no-retain").

Module clauses (text for insertion):
1) Scope of Module
This Module applies to Processing of Customer Data under the DPA where Customer has: (a) requested provenance commitments; or (b) supplied Consent Tokens with requests; or (c) is otherwise a regulated customer that requires specific audit evidence concerning outputs.

2) Provenance Metadata Logging
a) Redwood will persist Provenance Metadata for each Inference Output for a retention period not less than [90 days] and not to exceed [540 days], unless otherwise agreed in writing.
b) Provenance Metadata will include at minimum: model_id, model_version, execution_timestamp (UTC), node/region identifier, routing_decision_id, quantization_profile_id, input_hash (SHA-256 or equivalent non-reversible hash), and a processing_flags set (e.g., "consent:present", "fallback:used").
c) Customer acknowledges that Provenance Metadata is not a substitute for Customer retaining original request payloads where that is necessary to reconstruct semantic context; Redwood will not record full raw request content in Provenance Metadata except as permitted by the Data Handling Addendum or by specific agreement.

3) Consent Token Handling and Influence on Processing
a) When Customer supplies a Consent Token with a request, Redwood will: (i) persist an association between the Consent Token and the Provenance Metadata for the corresponding Inference Output; (ii) honor routing or retention instructions encoded in the Token to the extent technically feasible and lawful; and (iii) expose the Consent Token status in audit packages.
b) If a Consent Token instructs "no-retain", Redwood will mark the Provenance Metadata with "consent:no-retain" and limit retention of any associated content or ephemeral caches consistent with Section 4 (Retention); the input_hash may still be retained to satisfy auditability but must not be reversible.

c) Redwood may refuse to accept Consent Tokens that appear malformed or that instruct actions inconsistent with Redwood's security or operational constraints; in such cases Redwood will return an error code and logging in the API response as described in the API Contract Addendum.

4) Retention, Deletion, and Data Minimization
a) Provenance Metadata retention default: [180 days]. Customer may request a shorter retention period via the console or in writing, subject to minimum operational retention of [30 days] for diagnostics and abuse detection.
b) For requests flagged with "consent:no-retain", Redwood shall scope retention to technical minimums: retain non-reversible input_hash and routing identifiers for [30 days] then delete, unless Customer requests earlier deletion.
c) Where Customer has requested deletion for a specific Inference Output and provided the associated input_hash and execution_timestamp, Redwood will use reasonable efforts to locate and expunge associated Provenance Metadata and any derived artifacts within [30 days] and will confirm completion to Customer.

5) Audit, Evidence, and Verification
a) Redwood will provide an audit package on request that includes: (i) Provenance Metadata for the specified outputs; (ii) system logs demonstrating routing decisions and model-version mapping; (iii) cryptographic attestations of model version identifiers (where applicable). Audit requests shall be limited to [1] request per calendar quarter for standard subscribers and may be subject to audit fees for higher frequency or scope.
b) Forensic verification: Redwood will support an independent third-party auditor (reasonable notice and confidentiality obligations apply) to verify that Provenance Metadata and processing evidence align with the DPA commitments. Scope, timing, and cost allocation for third-party audits will be subject to a separate audit SOW.

6) Security Controls for Provenance Data
a) Provenance Metadata shall be treated as Confidential Information. Access controls: least-privilege role-based access with logging, separation of duties for retention/deletion operations, and MFA for privileged access.
b) Transmission and storage: Provenance Metadata in transit and at rest must be encrypted using industry standard algorithms (TLS 1.2+ for transit; AES-256 or equivalent for rest) unless Customer and Redwood agree otherwise.

7) Limitations and Exceptions
a) Where lawful governmental or legal obligations prevent Redwood from complying with a deletion or retention instruction, Redwood will notify Customer promptly unless prohibited by law and will provide reasonable assistance in mitigating data exposure.
b) Redwood's commitments do not require capture of sensitive personal data beyond what Customer supplies in the request; Customer remains responsible for ensuring lawful collection of end-user consent and for redaction of sensitive fields prior to submission if required by Customer policy.

8) Sample operational APIs and responses (implementation note)
- On request submission: API accepts header "X-Consent-Token: <opaque>" and returns X-Input-Hash and X-Execution-Timestamp for reference.
- Provenance retrieval API: /v1/provenance?input_hash=<>&ts=> returns the Provenance Metadata bundle for the authenticated Customer. Calls are rate-limited and logged.
- Deletion request: /v1/provenance/delete with proof of input_hash+timestamp returns asynchronous job id; job completion confirmed via webhook or polling endpoint.

9) Liability and indemnity (high level)
Customer and Redwood's liability in relation to Provenance Metadata shall be governed by the underlying DPA and Master Services Agreement. For avoidance of doubt, Redwood's obligation is to record and produce Provenance Metadata as described; Redwood does not warrant that Provenance Metadata alone will demonstrate compliance with Customer's legal obligations unless combined with Customer-held payloads and logs.

10) Change control and notices
Either party may request changes to the operational formats of Provenance Metadata with 60 days' notice; changes that materially alter retention, security or auditability will require mutual written agreement and may be subject to pricing adjustments.

Appendix A: Suggested short contract clause for insertion into DPA
"Provider shall maintain, for the retention period agreed in this Module, non-reversible provenance metadata sufficient to demonstrate the processing chain for an inference output (including model id/version, routing decision id, execution timestamp, and input_hash). Customer may supply Consent Tokens which Provider shall persist and honor as set out in the Module. Provider's obligations do not extend to retaining raw request payloads unless otherwise agreed."

Operational & legal questions for negotiation (notes to internal reviewers):
- Minimum/maximum retention defaults: customers will push for longer; ops wants hard caps for storage planning.
- Audit frequency and cost allocation: what is included for free vs billable?
- Cryptographic attestation format for model versions (signed manifests vs internal hashes).
- Handling of cross-border requests where Consent Token semantics differ by jurisdiction.

Document status and next steps:
- Drafted for legal/ops alignment. Request review from: Legal (privacy), Product (hosted-api + dedicated), Applied ML (model signing), and SRE (retention/eviction constraints).
- Action: schedule 30-min sync with Product and Applied ML to validate API headers and retention windows (owner: Nina Patel).

Placeholders to populate before external review:
- Final retention window values and minimum operational retention.
- Specific API error codes and webhook contract.
- Template SOW language for third-party audits and cost split.

End of document.
